newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME breakthrough.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in active trading on Friday due to overnight breaching of the key $2,000 resistance level on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,250 yuan ($2,319) per tonne, rising 250 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 19,200 and hit a high of 19,350.
November rose 80 to 18,780 yuan, December 250 to 18,950, January 270 to 19,200, March 240 to 19,320, April 190 to 19,300 and May 210 to 19,290.
Combined volume rose sharply to 95,150 tonnes from 48,970.
Copper opened higher and rose further before profit-taking and fresh buying pushing contracts off highs, but still up from Thursday's close.
Traders said the LME breakthrough encouraged long position holders early on, but strong selling emerged late in the session with concerns about over-supply of domestic spot copper.

"Many Shanghai investors were wary of following LME gains which they saw as a technical correction due to being long-term oversold," one trader said. "They are doubtful about copper's potential for further rises."

But some traders said that many long position holders offset their positions today and that copper is likely to test the 19,500-yuan level in the next few days if LME holds firmly above the $2,000 level.
"Copper could breach the 19,500-yuan level easily if LME keeps an upward trend in the short term," a second trader said.
Most investors are not optimistic about copper's long-term trend due to over-supply of spot copper despite their disagreement about the short-term trend.
"Copper has not broken out of a long-term downward path, which will put heavy pressure on long position holders," a third trader said.
Aluminium ended up. November rose 80 to 13,400 yuan per tonne, December 120 to 13,270 and January 170 to 13,270.
Combined volume rose to 1,030 tonnes from 490.
